title: Rigveda 4.35: To the Ribhus
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.35: To the Ribhus: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.35 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to the Ribhus. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 296r-297r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>i̱hopa̍ yāta śavaso napāta̱ḥ saudha̍nvanā ṛbhavo̱ māpa̍ bhūta | a̱smin hi va̱ḥ sava̍ne ratna̱dheya̱ṁ gama̱ntv indra̱m anu̍ vo̱ madā̍saḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Come hither, O ye Sons of Strength, ye R̥ibhus; stay not afar, ye Children of Sudhanvan. At this libation is your gift of treasure. Let gladdening draughts approach you after Indra's.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.35.2-5 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 296v
translation.original_text:
2āga̍nn ṛbhū̱ṇām i̱ha ra̍tna̱dheya̱m abhū̱t soma̍sya̱ suṣu̍tasya pī̱tiḥ | su̱kṛ̱tyayā̱ yat sva̍pa̱syayā̍ ca̱m̐ eka̍ṁ vica̱kra ca̍ma̱saṁ ca̍tu̱rdhā ||
3vy a̍kṛṇota cama̱saṁ ca̍tu̱rdhā sakhe̱ vi śi̱kṣety a̍bravīta | athai̍ta vājā a̱mṛta̍sya̱ panthā̍ṁ ga̱ṇaṁ de̱vānā̍m ṛbhavaḥ suhastāḥ ||
4ki̱mmaya̍ḥ svic cama̱sa e̱ṣa ā̍sa̱ yaṁ kāvye̍na ca̱turo̍ vica̱kra | athā̍ sunudhva̱ṁ sava̍na̱m madā̍ya pā̱ta ṛ̍bhavo̱ madhu̍naḥ so̱myasya̍ ||
5śacyā̍karta pi̱tarā̱ yuvā̍nā̱ śacyā̍karta cama̱saṁ de̍va̱pāna̍m | śacyā̱ harī̱ dhanu̍tarāv ataṣṭendra̱vāhā̍v ṛbhavo vājaratnāḥ ||
translation.text:
2Hither is come the R̥ibhus' gift of riches; here was the drinking of the well-pressed Soma, Since by dexterity and skill as craftsmen ye made the single chalice to be fourfold
3Ye made fourfold the chalice that was single: ye spake these words and said, O Friend, assist us; Then, Vâjas! gained the path of life eternal, deft-handed R̥ibhus, to the Gods' assembly.
4Out of what substance was that chalice fashioned which ye made fourfold by your art and wisdom? Now for the gladdening draught press out the liquor, and drink, O R̥ibhus, of die meath of Soma.
5Ye with your cunning made your Parents youthful; the cup, for Gods to drink, ye formed with cunning; With cunning, R̥ibhus, rich in treasure, fashioned the two swift Tawny Steeds who carry Indra.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.35.6-9 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 297r
translation.original_text:
6yo va̍ḥ su̱noty a̍bhipi̱tve ahnā̍ṁ tī̱vraṁ vā̍jāsa̱ḥ sava̍na̱m madā̍ya | tasmai̍ ra̱yim ṛ̍bhava̱ḥ sarva̍vīra̱m ā ta̍kṣata vṛṣaṇo mandasā̱nāḥ ||
7prā̱taḥ su̱tam a̍pibo haryaśva̱ mādhya̍ṁdina̱ṁ sava̍na̱ṁ keva̍laṁ te | sam ṛ̱bhubhi̍ḥ pibasva ratna̱dhebhi̱ḥ sakhī̱m̐r yām̐ i̍ndra cakṛ̱ṣe su̍kṛ̱tyā ||
8ye de̱vāso̱ abha̍vatā sukṛ̱tyā śye̱nā i̱ved adhi̍ di̱vi ni̍ṣe̱da | te ratna̍ṁ dhāta śavaso napāta̱ḥ saudha̍nvanā̱ abha̍vatā̱mṛtā̍saḥ ||
9yat tṛ̱tīya̱ṁ sava̍naṁ ratna̱dheya̱m akṛ̍ṇudhvaṁ svapa̱syā su̍hastāḥ | tad ṛ̍bhava̱ḥ pari̍ṣiktaṁ va e̱tat sam made̍bhir indri̱yebhi̍ḥ pibadhvam ||
translation.text:
6Whoso pours out for you, when days are closing, the sharp libation for your joy, O Vâjas, For him, O mighty R̥ibhus, ye, rejoicing, have fashioned wealth with plenteous store of heroes.
7Lord of Bay Steeds, at dawn thejuice thou drankest: thine, only thine, is the noonday libation. Now drink thou with the wealth-bestowing R̥ibhus, whom for their skill thou madest friends, O Indra.
8Ye, whom your artist skill hath raised to Godhead have sat you down above in heaven like falcons. So give us riches, Children of Sudhanvan, O Sons of Strength; ye have become immortal.
9The third libation, that bestoweth treasure, which ye have won by skill, ye dexterous-handed,– This drink hath been effused for you, O R̥ibhus . drink it with high delight, with joy like Indra's.
